items.claim: interpolateView ignores the anchor when both scales are negative
fitZoom, fitSize and useFitOnce skip the kit-wide zoom clamp
items.note: This is my call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md` under the new "Audit round forty-one" section. Tests that check the raw ratio now pass `{ min: 0, max: Infinity }`.

items.claim: sceneNodeClientRect loses precision far from the origin
useNodeOverlayFrame's view matrix loses precision far from the origin
useNodeOverlayFrame's toScreen and toLocal disagree once the node is gone
items.note: toScreen now also keeps the last invertible mapping while a live view flattens an axis, not only when the node is gone.

items.claim: useDecayLoop coasts forever on friction ≥ 1 or minSpeed ≤ 0
items.note: This is my call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`: it throws a RangeError, as `momentum()` does. `viewport.dragPan` checks its `inertia` when the drag is pressed, so the throw never comes from a pointer release.

items.claim: getVelocity ignores a pause before release
A one-axis zoom moves the other axis when that axis is out of range
items.note: in behavior, doc corrected in 0e5ebb5a87. zoomAt always brings every axis inside its clamp: a property law asserts it (`viewport.pbt.test.ts:131`), and labkit's `cameraZoom.ts` sets a zoom through `zoomAt(view, at, 1, { min: scale, max: scale })`. It was `axisZoomFactor`'s doc that was wrong.

items.claim: interpolateView loses precision when the scales differ by a hair just above the 1e-12 threshold
items.note: The pan is now `lerp(x0, x1, expm1(-t·ln r) / expm1(-ln r))`, which has no cancellation, so the threshold is gone.
